question: What is the biggest danger when someone has a severe case of watery diarrhoea?

options.A: Sudden increase in white blood cell count
options.B: Permanent damage to the stomach lining
options.C: Complete blockage of the large intestine
options.D: Rapid loss of water and electrolytes

explanation: Frequent watery stools quickly drain the body of vital fluids and salts, which can lead to dangerous dehydration before you know it. Great job keeping watch for this! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why is it sometimes a bad idea to immediately stop infectious diarrhoea with medicine?

options.A: It permanently destroys the muscles of the colon
options.B: It completely stops the absorption of all vitamins
options.C: It traps harmful toxins and bacteria inside the gut
options.D: It causes an immediate spike in blood pressure

explanation: When germs cause diarrhoea, your body tries to flush them out. Stopping the flow too soon just keeps the bad stuff trapped inside you! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the main job of motility inhibitor drugs in the gut?

options.A: Slow down gut movement to allow more water absorption
options.B: Coat the intestinal wall to prevent all nutrient uptake
options.C: Increase the speed of waste elimination
options.D: Kill infectious bacteria directly in the stomach

explanation: These drugs help calm down bowel movements. By slowing things down, your intestines get more time to soak up water from the stool. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h2)

question: How do adsorbent drugs help ease diarrhoea symptoms?

options.A: They bind to toxins and fluid on their surface
options.B: They increase blood flow to the intestinal lining
options.C: They paralyze the nerves of the large intestine
options.D: They stimulate the production of healthy gut bacteria

explanation: Think of adsorbents like a sponge in the gut—they grab onto bad toxins and extra liquid, carrying them safely out in the stool. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which drug is a commonly used over-the-counter motility inhibitor?
explanation: Loperamide acts directly on intestinal opioid receptors to slow down bowel movements and is widely available for self-treatment. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h3)

question: A patient with bloody diarrhoea and a fever takes loperamide. Why should the nurse step in and stop this?

options.A: Slowing bowel motility can trap invasive bacteria and worsen the infection
options.B: Loperamide will instantly neutralize all stomach acid and stop digestion
options.C: The combination will cause immediate and permanent kidney failure
options.D: Fever interferes with the chemical structure of opioid medications

explanation: When there's a serious bacterial infection, the body needs to get the germs out. Slowing down the gut traps the toxins inside and can make the patient much worse. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is a harmless, funny side effect you might see when a patient takes bismuth subsalicylate?

options.A: Temporary hair loss on the scalp
options.B: Bright yellow coloration of the urine
options.D: Darkening of the stool and tongue

explanation: Don't panic! Bismuth reacts with sulfur in your gut to create a harmless dark pigment that turns the tongue and stool black. It goes away soon after stopping the drug. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is it smart to space out other oral medications when a patient is taking an adsorbent drug?

options.A: Other medications will completely dissolve the adsorbent too quickly
options.B: Adsorbents can bind to other drugs and stop them from being absorbed
options.C: The adsorbent destroys the chemical makeup of all other pills
options.D: Combining them causes dangerous spikes in resting heart rate

explanation: Because adsorbents grab onto whatever is in the gut, they might accidentally trap other important medicines too, making them useless. Timing is everything! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h4)

question: How do antisecretory medications like racecadotril help manage diarrhoea?

options.A: They permanently paralyze the smooth muscles of the bowel
options.B: They reduce fluid and electrolyte secretion into the gut
options.C: They coat the entire stomach lining to block all acid
options.D: They kill all viruses present in the bloodstream

explanation: Instead of stopping gut movement, these drugs tell the intestines to stop pumping so much water and salt into your tummy. Clever, right? [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why are antibiotics NOT recommended for every single case of acute diarrhoea?

options.A: Antibiotics immediately stop the kidneys from producing urine
options.B: Most cases are viral or self-limiting, and routine use causes resistance
options.C: Bacteria are completely immune to all known pharmacological drugs
options.D: Antibiotics always cause immediate perforation of the large bowel

explanation: Most tummy bugs are viral and clear up on their own. Giving antibiotics too often just creates stubborn superbugs and harms good gut bacteria. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the secret behind why Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT) works so well?

options.A: Water absorption is stimulated by adding high amounts of sugar
options.B: Sodium and glucose transport together, pulling water into the body
options.C: Glucose completely paralyzes the nerves that cause bowel spasms
options.D: Sodium creates a thick barrier that blocks toxins from entering

explanation: Sodium and glucose team up in the gut wall. Even when you have diarrhoea, this special transport team helps pull water right back into your body. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h6)

question: What happens if a mother mixes an ORS packet in just a tiny cup of water instead of a full liter?

options.A: Complete blockage of the digestive tract due to thickness
options.B: Worse dehydration because the hypertonic solution draws water out of tissues
options.C: Immediate healing because the concentrated mixture acts much faster
options.D: Permanent numbness in the hands and feet from too much sodium

explanation: An overly concentrated mix is too salty! It pulls water *out* of the body's cells and into the gut, making dehydration much worse instead of better. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the easiest and most reliable way to track rapid fluid loss in a patient with diarrhoea?

options.C: Changes in skin color on the face
options.D: Total number of hours slept per night

explanation: Weight drops fast when you lose body water. Hopping on the scale daily is one of the best ways to catch dangerous dehydration early. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which sign tells you an elderly patient with severe diarrhoea is slipping into advanced dehydration?

options.A: Slow, deep breathing with warm, flushed skin
options.B: Dry mucous membranes and delayed capillary refill
options.C: High blood pressure and excessive saliva production
options.D: Increased muscle strength in the lower limbs

explanation: A dry mouth, sticky tongue, and sluggish refill when you press the fingernail mean there just isn't enough fluid circulating in the body anymore. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the single best way to stop infectious diarrhoea from spreading in a community?

options.A: Avoiding all physical exercise during warm weather
options.B: Drinking carbonated beverages instead of water
options.C: Proper handwashing with soap and water
options.D: Taking daily doses of over-the-counter loperamide

explanation: Simple soap and water break the cycle of germ transmission! Good hand hygiene is still your number one shield against stomach bugs. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h8)

question: Which symptom means a patient with diarrhoea should stop home treatment and see a doctor right away?

options.A: Mild rumbling sounds in the abdomen
options.C: Mild fatigue after a long day

explanation: Blood in the stool is a red flag! It usually points to a nasty bacterial infection or injury to the gut lining that needs professional medical help. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h8)
